Definition: from G4682 and G2795; to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition):--stir up.
BiblicalUsage: They stir up the people and the elders and the scribes against Stephen, and come upon him and catch him and bring him to the council. The stirring is a whole city set in motion together against one man, and a crowd that moves as one body can seize a man before anyone asks what he did.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that a stirred-up crowd is one of the oldest weapons against the truth, and I hold that Stephen's arrest began not with evidence but with a moving together.
